title: Machine-learning-assisted materials discovery using failed experiments
claim_supported: failed experiments can improve experimental decision models
study_design: 3955 complete notebook reactions plus prospective validation
key_result: model trained with dark reactions guided experiments and the selected prospective experiments achieved a high reported success rate
limitation: single materials system; source data were not literature-recovered

title: Target prediction utilising negative bioactivity data covering large chemical space
claim_supported: negative-inclusive target prediction can outperform an active-only comparator in the reported setting; independent benefit of experimentally measured negatives remains unproven
study_design: fivefold CV plus external WOMBAT evaluation; compare PubChem inactive + ChEMBL sphere-exclusion presumed negatives against ChEMBL active-only model
key_result: reported external mean PR-AUC 0.56 vs 0.45 and BEDROC 0.85 vs 0.76; paired Wilcoxon p=4.96e-05 and 7.08e-08; for 20 targets with >1000 confirmed inactives, adding sphere-exclusion samples improved WOMBAT precision in 19
limitation: training negative class mixes PubChem author-annotated assay inactives and ~11M presumed negatives; active-only model uses a different data composition; WOMBAT has no confirmed inactive labels and treats unannotated target pairs as inactive, so causal attribution to measured negatives is confounded

title: Negative chemical data boosts language models in reaction outcome prediction
claim_supported: a specialized reinforcement-learning pipeline can benefit from negative reaction outcomes in low-positive regimes; does not establish independent value for target-specific bioactivity negatives
study_design: RegioSQM controlled set (22 vs 220 positive training reactions, 748 negatives) and real HiTEA HTE set; five random splits plus different initializations
key_result: RegioSQM low-data RL improves positive accuracy versus fine-tuning and sustains USPTO performance; HiTEA low-data validation positive accuracy 0.644±0.015 versus 0.610±0.018 for fine-tuning, maximum 0.668 vs 0.628; top-10 test 0.441 vs 0.427. Full-positive setting also improves modestly (0.891±0.001 vs 0.877±0.001)
limitation: Specific RL + learned reward method, not a generic negative-data ablation. RegioSQM negatives are synthetically generated incorrect regioisomers, not failed wet-lab experiments. In HiTEA negatives are defined by measured yield ≤1%, but only 9/130 high-yield products have a negative-yield counterpart from identical reactants; threshold is used to show method applicability and low nonzero yields are not modeled continuously. Reaction prediction, not molecule-target bioactivity or literature recovery; authors note split instability and need more seeds/hyperparameter analysis

title: InertDB as a generative AI-expanded resource of biologically inactive small molecules from PubChem
claim_supported: negative source and chemical-space alignment affect downstream results; improvement over existing measured benchmark negatives is not consistent
study_design: same-test LIT-PCBA/MUV comparisons versus PubChem/ZINC random negatives and DeepCoy; separate replacement comparison with benchmark verified inactives
key_result: CIC/GIC beat random-source negatives or DeepCoy in some settings; replacing benchmark inactives had no significant LIT-PCBA effect (CIC p=.52, GIC p=.85) and a small MUV CIC gain (p=.0032)
limitation: CIC are broadly curated from PubChem rather than necessarily target-assay-specific; GIC are generated, not observed. ECFP4/RF and random holdouts do not establish temporal/assay-OOD or calibration benefit

title: How to Achieve Better Results Using PASS-Based Virtual Screening: Case Study for Kinase Inhibitors
claim_supported: target-specific measured active/inactive labels generally outperform cross-target merging that treats untested compounds as conditionally inactive, with exceptions
study_design: 152 human kinases; ChEMBL20 training; target-specific measured I-sets versus merged active/conditional-inactive MAI and active-only MA; ChEMBL23 external compound-target validation
key_result: I-sets generally outperformed MAI/MA in classification and BEDROC; 13 kinases favored merged sets for early recognition
limitation: does not isolate same-target incremental benefit of adding measured inactives; target aggregation and label semantics change together; PASS/MNA-specific

title: Target prediction utilising negative bioactivity data covering large chemical space
claim_supported: negative-inclusive target prediction can improve metrics relative to an active-only baseline
study_design: PubChem measured inactive plus ChEMBL sphere-exclusion presumed negatives compared with ChEMBL-active-only models; external WOMBAT evaluation
key_result: external WOMBAT mean PR-AUC .56 vs .45 and BEDROC .85 vs .76 reported
limitation: does not isolate experimental inactive contribution: negative labels mix observed and presumed negatives, training sources/sample composition differ, WOMBAT unannotated pairs treated as inactive

title: Inactive-enriched machine-learning models exploiting patent data improve structure-based virtual screening for PDL1 dimerizers
claim_supported: inactive-enriched scoring functions strongly outperform actives-only in one docking task; true inactives do not consistently outperform much larger random decoys
study_design: Same patent active sets; PubChem AID 2316 assay inactives, DeepCoy decoys, random ZINC decoys, active-only; separate TrueInactives and DeepCoy holdout test sets
key_result: Inactive-enriched models greatly outperform active-only; true-inactive training not significantly better than much larger random-decoy training; increasing random decoy quantity improved SBVS on true-inactive test
limitation: single target and docking-derived 3D representations; inactive counts vary greatly; active-only classification is a high/low potency split, so effect cannot be isolated to experimental negative status or generalized to ligand-only QSAR

title: Hidden bias in the DUD-E dataset leads to misleading performance of deep learning in structure-based virtual screening
claim_supported: negative construction can create spurious model gains
study_design: CNN structure-based tests plus ligand-topology controls
key_result: showed that strong scores can be driven by analogue and decoy bias
limitation: negative evidence about benchmark validity rather than a positive utility result

title: DEEPScreen: high performance drug-target interaction prediction with convolutional neural networks using 2-D structural compound representations
claim_supported: measured inactive records and leakage-aware splits are feasible baselines
study_design: target-specific ChEMBL datasets with scaffold or temporal evaluation
key_result: explicitly analyzed negative selection bias and compared non-random evaluations
limitation: does not isolate the effect of literature-recovered context-rich negatives

title: Benchmarking compound activity prediction for real-world drug discovery applications
claim_supported: downstream gains must be tested at assay level
study_design: CARA zero-shot few-shot virtual-screening and lead-optimization tasks
key_result: demonstrates that task setting and assay structure change measured performance
limitation: benchmark does not test recovered negative evidence

title: Enzyme promiscuity prediction using hierarchy-informed multi-label classification
claim_supported: For a BRENDA enzyme-molecule compatibility task, does explicit known-inhibitor supervision outperform treating the same inhibitor observations as unlabeled?
study_design: 25,872 BRENDA substrate-positive and 13,087 inhibitor interactions across 983 EC numbers; same inhibitor compounds are similarity-weighted unlabeled without inhibitor supervision or explicitly labeled as inhibitors; random/realistic splits, inhibitor/unlabeled test sets; EPP-HMCNF with versus without inhibitor supervision
key_result: On reduced data under realistic split, EPP-HMCNF AUROC 0.849 to 0.857, AP 0.131 to 0.149, and R-PREC 0.111 to 0.126 after inhibitor supervision
limitation: Same-record supervision comparison suggests utility beyond simply adding new molecules, but inhibitors are not experimentally confirmed non-substrate pairs; task/model-specific, not independently rerun, and does not test historical literature-recovered no-detect records

title: Extremely Randomized Machine Learning Methods for Compound Activity Prediction
claim_supported: Does benchmark performance change when the negative class uses target-specific ChEMBL threshold-inactives, DUD decoys, or both?
study_design: Same seven targets, six fingerprints and four classifier families; compare actives-vs-true-inactives, actives-vs-DUD 1/2 and mixed true-inactives+DUD; ChEMBL thresholds Ki/IC50 for active and inactive classes
key_result: Table 5 best-fingerprint BAC is approximately 0.875–0.919 on measured-inactive sets, 0.899–0.967 on mixed sets, and 0.996–1.000 on DUD-decoy sets
limitation: Shows substantial benchmark difficulty/source sensitivity and warns against treating decoy performance as assay-negative performance; not a matched-size negative-source ablation and does not show incremental value from adding measured inactives
